title: POC Weekly Sync — runtime patch readout & routing decisions
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on the recent inference-runtime patch, routing fallback behavior during degraded egress, and telemetry gaps. Team agreed on a controlled canary, additional soak testing, and a short action list: perf spreadsheet, security docs, and a timeline for next upgrade window.
topics: next steps and decision on upgrade window
action_items: Samir (Redwood SE): run 12h soak with kv-cache priming and share perf CSV — due 2027-12-01
Maya (Customer): validate SR-IOV config on two on-prem nodes and report kernel logs — due 2027-12-02
Claire (AE): send updated pricing/commit options and pilot addendum — due 2027-11-30
Elena (Customer Security): request SOC2 and network diagram, Redwood to provide link — due 2027-12-03
next_steps: Canary the runtime-patch to 10% traffic in us-west-2 on Tuesday (2027-12-05)
Run extended soak with realistic token distribution and long-context prompts
Share perf/latency spreadsheet and telemetry dashboard link
Security team to review KMS/HSM notes and firewall requirements
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Claire M., Samir P., Ivy Z., John R., Maya L., Ravi S., Elena G.

Summary (auto): quick readout on runtime patch, fallback routing observed in last window, action items captured.

[00:00] Claire (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have the usual crew, we'll go through the patch readout, samir will take the perf bits and then open Q&A.
[00:22] John (NetOps - HearthBridge): cool, thanks, and sorry i was late, traffic at the colo.
[00:30] Samir (Redwood SE): no worries — i'll kick off with the runtime-patch, we rolled v1.2.3 to the canary cluster last thursday, it includes a couple of fixes: improved kv-cache priming, better batching heuristics, and a guard for out-of-memory during long context streaming.
[00:55] Maya (Platform Eng): can you remind us which node types you targeted? we have a mix of 32GB A100-ish and some older 24GB cards onprem.
[01:10] Samir (Redwood SE): yes, the canary was on two 32GB nodes in the private vpc overlay, we did not touch the 24GB cards yet — that was deliberate to avoid compaction issues.
[01:28] Elena (Security): quick question — the patch touches memory allocation paths, any change to encryption or KMS calls?
[01:40] Samir (Redwood SE): nope, no KMS surface changed, encryption flows unchanged. we did add extra telemetry hooks which emit a new metric (runtime.alloc.fail_rate) to internal metrics.
[01:55] Ravi (CTO): we saw a couple of timeouts during last night’s run, routing fallback kicked in — can you explain what you observed?
[02:10] Samir (Redwood SE): yeah so during a burst during our egress shaping test, the on-prem egress link briefly saturated, and our smart routing sent ~7% of requests to the fallback model variant (lower-quant profile). latency for those requests rose ~120ms but cost dropped a bit. the issue was the egress queue filling and the kernel pacing interacting with our batching heuristics.
[02:36] John (NetOps): right, on our side we saw TLS session churn and some retransmits, the MTU sizing looked off on one switch, which prolonged the backlog.
[02:50] Claire (AE): ok, so that's network-congestion induced fallback — is that correct?
[02:58] Samir (Redwood SE): yes, it's an interplay of egress shaping + batching. when the egress drops below threshold, we apply the routing policy to push to cheaper variant to keep tail latency bounded. it did what it was supposed to, but we want to reduce the number of fallbacks.
[03:15] Maya (Platform Eng): is there a way to bias the routing policy to prefer region-local replicas over quantized variants? sometimes cost tradeoffs are less acceptable.
[03:29] Samir (Redwood SE): good point — we can tune the policy to prefer same-region replicas if latencySLO is higher priority. that will of course increase token-costs under heavy egress pressure.
[03:44] Claire (AE): i think HearthBridge prefers latency for production flows, cost for the background batch jobs. we should map routes by traffic class.
[03:56] Ravi (CTO): agreed. for the pilot we can accept a small cost bump if tail latency improves.
[04:05] Ivy (CSM): Samir, can you share the perf spreadsheet with the cost delta for different fallback thresholds? customers always like numbers.
[04:15] Samir (Redwood SE): yes i will — short-term i have the canary CSV, i'll add a column for cost delta and push by monday.
[04:26] John (NetOps): on SR-IOV testing — we ran a quick pass in lab and the NIC offloads look good but we had to disable a jumbo frame setting to avoid reassembly issues. that may explain part of the MTU mismatch.
[04:44] Maya (Platform Eng): are we comfortable enabling SR-IOV in the pilot? it's supposed to reduce CPU overhead for egress.
[04:53] Samir (Redwood SE): we recommend it for high-throughput setups but want logs from two on-prem nodes first. i asked john to collect dmesg and kernel logs for any offload errors.
[05:05] John (NetOps): will do. i'll attach them to the ticket.
[05:12] Elena (Security): on telemetry — we noticed some gaps, the long-tail percentiles for token latency are missing between 10PM and 2AM. it looks like ingestion dropped.
[05:24] Samir (Redwood SE): yes, we uncovered a race where our agent rotated logs during a high IO window and the collector missed a batch. patch v1.2.3 includes a retry for the agent and a buffering improvement.
[05:39] Elena (Security): good, also please add an audit log marker when fallback is triggered — we need that for our compliance showback.
[05:50] Samir (Redwood SE): understood, we can emit an audit event: fallback.triggered with routing_reason and model_variant. we'll include that in the next telemetry push.
[06:03] Ravi (CTO): from a timeline perspective, what's your recommended upgrade window if we want to push v1.2.3 to 50%?
[06:14] Samir (Redwood SE): recommended path: run a 12–24h soak on canary, then canary to 10% traffic for 48h (region us-west-2), if no issues extend to 50% and run a targeted onprem upgrade for the 32GB nodes. given that, earliest 50% could be Dec 7-8 if soak looks healthy.
[06:38] Claire (AE): ok that gives us a schedule — we'll coordinate with devops for the window.
[06:45] John (NetOps): one more note — when fallback happened we saw increased traffic to our egress proxy which caused CPU spikes, so maybe we should also throttle fallback ramp rate.
[06:57] Samir (Redwood SE): yep, we can add a ramp control so fallback doesn't go from 0 to 20% in a single minute — settable parameter.
[07:07] Maya (Platform Eng): is there any change to observability retention? we need longer retention for tail percentiles to do regressions.
[07:17] Ivy (CSM): we can discuss extended retention as an add-on—Claire will follow up on pricing.
[07:25] Ravi (CTO): security question — do you keep audit logs in our VPC or do they get forwarded to Redwood? we want custody.
[07:34] Elena (Security): yeah i second that, custody is a big ask.
[07:39] Claire (AE): plan is logs remain in your VPC; we ship salted aggregates to Redwood console but raw audit logs can stay customer-managed. i'll attach the network diagram and the doc describing log flows.
[07:52] Elena (Security): please include the KMS notes too, and any HSM integration details.
[07:58] Samir (Redwood SE): will do — no HSM change in v1.2.3, but we have a note on KMS rotation and key policies.
[08:07] John (NetOps): about the MTU mismatch, our switch team is going to schedule a config change — when you run the next canary could you avoid jumbo frames just in case?
[08:18] Samir (Redwood SE): yes we'll configure the canary to standard mtu during the canary window.
[08:24] Claire (AE): sounds good. any blockers from the customer's side to the schedule?
[08:30] Maya (Platform Eng): we need the SR-IOV logs and the perf spreadsheet — once we have those we can greenlight the soak.
[08:38] John (NetOps): i'll upload logs by monday EOD.
[08:42] Samir (Redwood SE): i'll share the perf CSV and an annotated dashboard link.
[08:48] Claire (AE): ok, let's capture the decision points.
[08:51] --- brief silence / typing ---
[09:00] Claire (AE): quick commercial note — if you prefer committed reserved capacity for nodes that affects pricing; i'll put both options in the addendum.
[09:10] Ravi (CTO): please do. we'll evaluate.
[09:14] Maya (Platform Eng): regarding fallback bias, let's make the default prefer region-local replicas for production and cheaper variants for batch windows. that should be configurable per route.
[09:26] Samir (Redwood SE): agreed, we'll supply a routing policy template for traffic classes.
[09:32] Elena (Security): one more ask — can the fallback audit event include a correlation id so we can tie it to request logs?
[09:41] Samir (Redwood SE): yes correlation_id is already part of our request envelope, we'll include it.
[09:47] Claire (AE): ok great. are there any other risks we should call out before finishing?
[09:52] John (NetOps): risk: if the egress proxy CPU spikes during fallback, we may hit headroom limits; mitigation: throttle fallback and increase proxy headroom during test.
[10:05] Ravi (CTO): risk: if SR-IOV behaves differently on older kernels we need a rollback plan — i want the kernel logs up front.
[10:16] Samir (Redwood SE): we'll maintain a rollback playbook and a canary cutoff threshold.
[10:22] Ivy (CSM): i'll schedule a follow-up check-in after the soak — same time next week?
[10:30] Claire (AE): yes, same time next week works for us.
[10:35] Maya (Platform Eng): one last question — are there any known regressions in output quality with the lower-quant variant? we noticed minor truncation in dense prompts last week.
[10:47] Samir (Redwood SE): lower-quant tends to slightly shorten completions on long-form generation. our optimize team runs evals; i'll attach a quality delta table. for production prompts we'll mark them to avoid fallback unless absolutely necessary.
[11:03] Ravi (CTO): perfect. thanks everyone.
[11:08] Claire (AE): recap / next steps: Samir runs 12h soak and shares perf CSV; John uploads kernel/NIC logs; Claire sends pricing addendum and security docs; Elena to review SOC2/KMS notes. follow-up next week same time.
[11:30] Meeting end.
